motion: Does analytic idealism explain consciousness and reality better than materialism?

routes.speaker: Bernardo Kastrup
routes.position: Analytic idealism better explains consciousness and reality.

bridges.statement: Analytic idealism explains consciousness and reality more coherently and parsimoniously than materialism.
Consciousness is the directly known ontological primitive, while matter is its extrinsic appearance.
Dissociation within transpersonal consciousness explains individual minds and their physical appearances.
Neuroscience, biology, and ordinary causal interaction are compatible with idealism's appearance account.
Consciousness must be distinguished from intelligence and attributed cautiously by organismic analogy.

routes.speaker: Tom Jump
routes.position: Materialism remains a viable explanation of consciousness and reality.

bridges.statement: Materialism remains viable because idealism has not shown a decisive comparative explanatory advantage.
Present ignorance about mind-brain relations does not establish an in-principle impossibility.
Idealism may relocate emergence and boundary problems while assuming more than cautious materialism.
Composition, functional organization, and artificial realizations make material emergence plausible.
The causal dependence of experience on physical interventions favors or at least preserves materialist explanations.
